title: InfiniTime (PineTime) heart rate: autocorrelation (0.11.0-1.12.0) vs FFT (1.13.0-1.16.1)
caveat: Algorithm layer only: Drift compiles InfiniTime's Ppg.cpp (and its Biquad/Ptagc/arduinoFFT dependencies) and replays recorded PPG counts through it. Sensor-driver changes (HRS3300 gain 64x -> 8x in 1.9.0, the 1.13.0 LED-current/resolution/wait retune, atomic reads in 1.15.0) alter the raw counts themselves and the HeartRateTask layer (timing, 1.16 background measurement) alters when values are shown; neither can be replayed from a recording. The public PPG data are not HRS3300 data: they are rescaled to HRS3300-like counts under stated assumptions. Results describe the algorithms on this data, not the PineTime as shipped.
caveats: Algorithm layer only: Drift compiles InfiniTime's Ppg.cpp (and its Biquad/Ptagc/arduinoFFT dependencies) and replays recorded PPG counts through it. Sensor-driver changes (HRS3300 gain 64x -> 8x in 1.9.0, the 1.13.0 LED-current/resolution/wait retune, atomic reads in 1.15.0) alter the raw counts themselves and the HeartRateTask layer (timing, 1.16 background measurement) alters when values are shown; neither can be replayed from a recording. The public PPG data are not HRS3300 data: they are rescaled to HRS3300-like counts under stated assumptions. Results describe the algorithms on this data, not the PineTime as shipped.
Ground truth is ECG R-peaks from a different sensor/subject population (8 subjects, exercise); exercise PPG is dominated by motion artifacts and InfiniTime's algorithms use no accelerometer.
Only 8 subjects: the subject-level bootstrap interval is wide and is the primary one; the window-level interval treats autocorrelated windows as independent and is optimistic.
Scaling of the public PPG to HRS3300 counts is an assumption (see scaling_sensitivity).
The six real PineTime recordings have no ground truth: they support agreement statements only.

provenance.toolchain: zig c++ 0.16.0 -std=c++17 -O2 (libc++), MSVC 14.44 cross-check in recon

infinitime-fork-ppg.license: data files unlabelled (repo GPL-3.0); agreement checks only

provenance.scaling: anti-aliased polyphase resample from 256 Hz to the generation's native rate; robust AC sigma 25 counts (1.4826*MAD of the 0.5-4 Hz band), median shifted to 3600 counts, rounded, clipped to 0..32767

generations.label: 0.11.0-1.12.0 autocorrelation, 24 Hz
generations.algorithm: wasp-os time-domain autocorrelation (Biquad HPF -> Ptagc AGC -> Biquad LPF -> trough search), 200-sample buffer, bpm = 60*24*4/lag

generations.label: 1.13.0-1.16.1 FFT, 10 Hz
generations.algorithm: Ceimour's FFT (arduinoFFT): 64-sample Hann window every 0.5 s, 3-spectrum average, peak search 30-240 bpm, running mean over 20 outputs

generations.label: 1.12.0 null control of gen A
generations.algorithm: wasp-os time-domain autocorrelation (Biquad HPF -> Ptagc AGC -> Biquad LPF -> trough search), 200-sample buffer, bpm = 60*24*4/lag
generations.kept_because: null control: last gen-A variant (1.12.0), must equal gen A

agreement_real_pinetime.scope: agreement only: the recordings have no ground truth, so nothing here measures accuracy
agreement_real_pinetime.input_handling: The stitched 10 Hz stream is fed to gen B as recorded. Gen A assumes 24 Hz, so the same stream is resampled 10 -> 24 Hz (polyphase 12/5). This is an assumption: a PineTime running gen A would have produced different raw counts (other gain, rate, LED settings).
